text.p: Following are highlights of some of the main stories in Croatian dailies. Reuters has not verified these reports nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- The government decides to found a company charged with building and managing the Rijeka-Zagreb-Gorican motorway.
- Meat producers may cut prices of poultry, pork and beef between five and 13 percent from next week provided fodder prices also decrease.
- America threatens Milosevic with sanctions if he fails to come true on commitments to hand over war criminals.
- Deputy PM Borislav Skegro receives the new Canadian ambassador to Croatia, Donald Smith.
- Education system in Eastern Slavonia integrated with the mainstream system pending the region's reintegration.
- New director of the Rijeka port vows to win back cargo and restructure the company.

- The cabinet confirms a three-percent increase in the electricity price for households from July. Director of the electricity board (HEP), Damir Begovic, says HEP had no other choice to cover its higher costs due to inflation.
- 26 people injured in a tram clash in Zagreb, two hospitalised. Trams to run past the main train station again from next week after extensive reconstruction.

- Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic puts this year's wheat crop at around 840,000 tonnes, most of which is already in government silos. Dominikovic says maize crop may be a record one in the past 10 years.
- First-half budget report shows revenues of 17.8 billion kuna and spending at 44.76 percent of the annual plan. Some 1.25 million kuna spent on official cars.

- Commentary: Everyone please with the outcome of the talks in Split between Franjo Tudjman and Alija Izetbegovic. U.S. envoys confirm the international community will not relent on the implementation of the Dayton peace accord.
- Croatia has made sure it has enough bread from this year's wheat crop, says Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
